Both Riyadh and Baghdad traced the attack to Iraqi territory, where Iran-backed militias operate, prompting the Iraqi government to dismiss a senior military commander on Saturday. While Saudi Arabia [USN:S8N44107S TEXT:"withheld immediate military retaliation"] following an appeal from Iraq's prime minister, Riyadh asserted its right to defend its sovereignty and critical infrastructure. Broadening the geopolitical fallout, U.S. President Donald Trump on Saturday directly blamed Iran for the strikes on the conduit, which serves as the kingdom's primary export alternative to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The disruption highlights persistent vulnerabilities in regional oil infrastructure; prior attacks on Saudi energy facilities previously slashed crude output by 2.3 million barrels per day to a three-decade low of 6 million bpd, according to the International Energy Agency. Elsewhere in the Gulf, Qatar's benchmark index (.QSI) bucked the regional trend, rising 0.2% on the back of gains in petrochemical producer Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA) . Gulf foreign ministers plan to [USN:FWN4520ZF TEXT:"meet"] their Iranian counterpart in an Oman-backed push to secure an interim deal on managing traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

item.title: Russian drone attack injures five in Ukraine's Odesa, officials say
item.description: At least five people were wounded in a Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Odesa on Sunday morning, officials said, a day after strikes on the city killed two people.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least five people were wounded in a Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Odesa on Sunday morning, officials said, a day after strikes on the city killed two people. "Residential areas were damaged in several districts of the city. Authorities are assessing the full extent of the damage," the head of Odesa military administration, Serhiy Lysak, said on Telegram. Odesa, home to Ukraine's main port hub, has faced persistent Russian missile and drone attacks in recent months, forcing the closure of seaports crucial to Ukrainian exports. According to officials, a Russian drone [USN:L1N45403Z TEXT:"struck the city"] on Saturday morning, hitting an apartment building and killing two people while injuring 26. Several other regions were also targeted in attacks in western Ukraine that continued through the night and into the morning, regional authorities said on Sunday. They did not immediately report civilian casualties.

item.title: MLB roundup: Mariners clobber A's by franchise-record 18 runs
item.description: The Seattle Mariners set a franchise record for largest victory margin as well as season bests for runs and hits in a 19-1 rout of the Athletics on Saturday night in West Sacramento, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Mariners set a franchise record for largest victory margin as well as season bests for runs and hits in a 19-1 rout of the Athletics on Saturday night in West Sacramento, Calif. Cole Young homered and drove in five runs and Randy Arozarena went deep and had four RBIs for the Mariners. Among their 23 hits were rookie Michael Arroyo's first major league homer and home runs for Dominic Canzone and J.P. Crawford. Weston Wilson had a career-best five hits while Young, Arroyo (three RBIs), Josh Naylor and Julio Rodriguez had three hits apiece for Seattle. Right-hander Bryan Woo (12-9) continued his mastery against the Athletics by allowing one unearned run and three hits over six innings. He struck out five and walked two to improve to 9-1 in 12 career starts against the A's. The Athletics lost for just the third time in 10 games. All-Star Shea Langeliers (knee) was activated prior to the game and went 1-for-3 with the lone RBI. Gage Jump (6-11) gave up five runs and five hits over two innings. Mets 12, Yankees 2 Francisco Lindor, Luis Torrens and rookie Carson Benge homered off Gerrit Cole, and the visiting Mets rolled to a 12-2 victory over the Yankees. Lindor added a grand slam in the eighth as the Mets won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 22-13 since their big selloff at last month's trade deadline by hitting Cole hard again. Rookie Zac Thornton (4-5) allowed two runs on five hits in a career-high-tying seven innings. Cole was tagged for five runs on nine hits (three home runs) in 4 1/3 innings after allowing four homers in Sunday's loss at San Diego. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter as he matched his second-shortest outing since returning from Tommy John surgery on May 22. Tigers 11, Rockies 7 Hao-Yu Lee sparked a seven-run, eighth-inning rally with a double and capped it with a two-run triple as host Detroit beat struggling Colorado. Lee had three hits, scored twice and drove in three runs. Max Clark supplied three hits while scoring a run and knocking in another, and Kevin McGonigle added a solo homer. Hunter Goodman blasted a three-run homer for the Rockies, who have lost six straight. Tigers starter Andrew Sears gave up four runs and seven hits in 4 1/3 innings. Colorado starter Tanner Gordon allowed four runs and 10 hits in four innings. Marlins 4, Dodgers 3 Graham Pauley slugged a two-run homer and Otto Lopez smacked a go-ahead RBI single in a three-run second inning as host Miami defeated Los Angeles to end the Dodgers' eight-game winning streak. The Marlins' bullpen allowed just two hits and one run in 5 1/3 innings. Miami snapped a four-game losing skid. The Marlins are just 2-7 over their past nine games. Max Muncy and Mookie Betts -- each with a solo homer -- led Los Angeles' offense. Muncy has 28 dingers this season. Betts has 20. Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman returned to action after missing two games due to knee soreness. Freeman went 0-for-4. Rays 3, Astros 2 Pinch hitter Nick Madrigal produced a tie-breaking sacrifice fly, Bryan Baker recorded his major league-leading 40th save and first-place Tampa Bay edged Houston in St. Petersburg, Fla. Richie Palacios had a single and two RBIs while Victor Mesa singled, scored and walked twice as the Rays stretched their lead over the New York Yankees in the American League East to four games. Starter Ian Seymour had a dominant stretch after allowing a run in the first inning but failed to win in his sixth straight appearance, five of them starts. The left-hander finished with two runs allowed on four hits over six innings. He whiffed 10 and walked one. Tyler Wells (5-2) followed Seymour with a scoreless seventh. White Sox 6, Cardinals 5 Randal Grichuk hit a go-ahead two-run home run with two outs in the top of the ninth inning to help Chicago beat host St. Louis and snap a four-game losing streak. Grichuk went deep with a 1-2 count against closer Riley O'Brien, taking a sinker just over the fence to the opposite field in right, with outfielder Victor Scott II also losing his glove over the fence. Grichuk's 13th home run, against the team that brought him to the majors, trumped a tie-breaking solo shot by Cardinals rookie Leo Bernal against Grant Taylor in the bottom of the eighth. Another former Cardinals player, right-hander Jordan Hicks (3-2), walked a batter but also got one out for the victory. Bryan Hudson got three outs for his eighth save. Rangers 6, Diamondbacks 2 Wyatt Langford hit a 435-foot homer to open a six-run fifth inning, Elias Diaz had three hits and an RBI, and Texas beat Arizona in Phoenix to even their three-game series. Rangers right-hander Nathan Eovaldi, activated from the injured list Saturday, gave up one run over 2 2/3 innings of relief in his first appearance since Aug. 7, though he did not factor in the decision. Brandon Nimmo had two doubles and an RBI, and Josh Jung had two hits and an RBI for Texas. Jung was also activated from the injured list Saturday. Langford added a double. Cubs 4, Pirates 3 Nico Hoerner was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded in the eighth inning to force in the go-ahead run as Chicago pulled out a victory over visiting Pittsburgh. Pedro Ramirez had a double and a home run, and Michael Busch hit a solo shot for the Cubs. Ryan Rolison (9-1) allowed one hit in 1 2/3 scoreless innings to earn the win. Ryan Zeferjahn struck out Bryan Reynolds looking for the final out and his sixth save. Ryan O'Hearn hit a three-run home run, and Paul Skenes allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings for the Pirates. Braves 12, Phillies 2 Michael Harris II and Ronald Acuna Jr. each homered and right-hander Tyler Mahle produced another strong start to lead Atlanta to a win over visiting Philadelphia, clinching the three-game series. The Braves now hold a six-game lead over the two-time division champion Phillies in the National League East. Harris was 4-for-5 with a three-run homer, his 25th, and two runs. Acuna was 3-for-3 with a home run and a walk, two runs scored and two RBIs. Mahle (6-10) matched his season high by pitching seven innings and allowed one run on six hits. Tim Mayza was Philadelphia's replacement starter for Jesus Luzardo, who had to be skipped because of shoulder soreness. It was the fifth time the left-hander had been used as an opener. He pitched three scoreless innings with two hits before being lifted. Brewers 13, Reds 9 Garrett Mitchell's bat remained scorching hot as the Milwaukee center fielder went 4-for-5 with four RBIs, helping the host Brewers break a record as they defeated Cincinnati. Mitchell, who went 3-for-5 with a grand slam Friday, got all four hits in the first five innings, with a two-run homer in the first, and a two-run double that capped a five-run fifth. Cooper Pratt doubled while going 3-for-5, while Brice Turang (2-for-4) and William Contreras also homered in the win. Juan Brito (3-for-4) hit his second home run and drove in three for the Reds, who lost their fifth straight. Eugenio Suarez hit his 23rd home run as part of a 3-for-4 night with three runs scored and two RBIs, and JJ Bleday broke an 0-for-20 streak with a 2-for-5 performance that included two runs scored and an RBI. Red Sox 5, Royals 1 Ranger Suarez tossed his second straight seven-inning start and Boston scored in its final three at-bats en route to a win over visiting Kansas City. Suarez (7-4) struck out eight, scattered five hits and allowed one run while completing his seven frames in 96 pitches as the Red Sox snapped their three-game losing streak. Roman Anthony, Adley Rutschman and Nick Sogard each had multiple hits while Wilyer Abreu hit a two-run double that gave Boston a sixth-inning lead it would not relinquish. Carter Jensen's 24th home run of the season marked the only scoring for the Royals, who opened the series with a win Friday. Blue Jays 7, Orioles 3 Alejandro Kirk belted a two-run home run and had three RBIs to help Toronto defeat visiting Baltimore. The teams have split the first two of the three-game series in their pursuit of an American League playoff spot. The Blue Jays are one game behind the Cleveland Guardians for the third and final AL wild-card spot. The Orioles are three behind. Brett Bateman added a solo shot for Toronto. Kyle Bradish (7-14) allowed five runs and eight hits in three innings for Baltimore. Padres 7, Giants 6 Jackson Merrill and Fernando Tatis Jr. hit home runs, Michael King overcame a shaky start to complete seven innings, and San Diego overcame host San Francisco for a sixth consecutive win. Dustin Harris drove in three runs and Xander Bogaerts had four hits for the Padres, who now sit a game and a half ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third and final National League wild-card playoff spot. Giants starter Cesar Perdomo (0-1) couldn't finish the fifth, having allowed five runs and 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings. King (11-9) was pulled with a 7-3 lead after the seventh, having set down 16 of the final 18 batters he faced. He was charged with three runs on five hits, striking out four and walking none. Nationals 6, Angels 5 Harry Ford drove in the winning run with an infield grounder and Washington survived another blown save to beat visiting Los Angeles. With one out, Daylen Lile was intentionally walked by Jose Fermin (4-3). Runners CJ Abrams and Lile executed a double steal and, with the infield in, Angels shortstop Zach Neto booted Ford's grounder and Abrams scored the winning run. Jack Sinclair (1-0) pitched 1 1/3 innings for the win. Los Angeles trailed 4-0 entering the eighth but scored three runs in the eighth and two more in the ninth as the Nationals added to their major league record with their 39th blown save of the season. Andres Chaparro singled in Jose Tena to tie the game in the ninth. Twins 4, Guardians 3 Emmanuel Rodriguez hit a home run in his first big-league plate appearance and Minnesota held on for a win over Cleveland in Minneapolis. Royce Lewis went 1-for-3 with an RBI for the Twins, who also got RBIs from Kody Clemens and Victor Caratini, all in Minnesota's four-run third inning. Twins left-hander Connor Prielipp (5-7) picked up his second victory in his past three starts, giving up three runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings, Travis Bazzana finished 1-for-3 with an RBI for the Guardians, who dropped to 1 1/2 games behind the Chicago White Sox in the American League Central. Steven Kwan and Brayan Rocchio each drove in a run. Franco Aleman (0-1) was pelted for four runs on five hits in two-thirds of an inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyiv a attaqué des camions de diesel et mis en danger Zaporijjia, selon le chef du nucléaire russe
item.description: Le directeur de la société d'État russe chargée de l'énergie nucléaire a accusé dimanche l'Ukraine d'avoir attaqué des camions transportant du diesel, tuant deux militaires russes et compromettant délibérément la sécurité de la centrale nucléaire de Zaporijjia, en Ukraine, contrôlée par la Russie.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le directeur de la société d'État russe chargée de l'énergie nucléaire a accusé dimanche l'Ukraine d'avoir attaqué des camions transportant du diesel, tuant deux militaires russes et compromettant délibérément la sécurité de la centrale nucléaire de Zaporijjia, en Ukraine, contrôlée par la Russie. Alexeï Likhachev a déclaré que l'attaque avait eu lieu vendredi et avait également fait des blessés parmi d'autres soldats russes. La centrale de Zaporijjia, la plus grande d'Europe avec ses six réacteurs, a été prise par les forces russes au cours des premières semaines de la guerre en Ukraine, qui a éclaté en février 2022. Chaque camp accuse régulièrement l'autre de mener des actions mettant en danger la sécurité du site et augmentant le risque d'accident nucléaire. Alexeï Likhachev a publié un communiqué indiquant que les forces ukrainiennes avaient lancé vendredi "une série de frappes combinées" contre des camions-citernes approvisionnant la centrale en diesel. "Les frappes ont touché très près du périmètre du site de la centrale", a-t-il déclaré. "Deux militaires ont été tués et un grand nombre de soldats russes ont été blessés, dont certains gravement. Ils participaient tous à cette mission purement civile." Le carburant revêt une importance cruciale pour la centrale de Zaporijjia, car les générateurs diesel fournissent l'électricité nécessaire au refroidissement du combustible nucléaire dans les réacteurs lorsque les deux connexions électriques externes de la centrale sont hors service. Elles l'ont été pendant près de trois semaines en août et en septembre. L'Ukraine exige que la Russie se retire de la centrale et en restitue l'exploitation à Kyiv, une demande rejetée par Moscou. Les réacteurs de la centrale sont à l'arrêt depuis 2022. L'Agence internationale de l'énergie atomique (AIEA), organisation internationale sous l'égide de l'Onu, a déployé une équipe d'observateurs présente en permanence sur le site de Zaporijjia, ainsi que dans les trois autres centrales ukrainiennes en activité. L'agence a joué à plusieurs reprises le rôle d'intermédiaire en cas de différends et a contribué le mois dernier à la mise en place d'un cessez-le-feu local afin de permettre la réalisation de réparations et le rétablissement des liaisons électriques externes.

JAKARTA: Indonesian rescuers were searching on Sunday for 130 people from a passenger ship that sank in the Java Sea after 113 others were evacuated, the country’s search and rescue agency said, adding that six people had died.

An Indonesian passenger ship carrying 243 people, including 30 crew members, was reported missing after losing contact with authorities early on Sunday during bad weather, the search and rescue agency said.

The Virgo Transport 8 ship set sail on Saturday from the East Java city of Surabaya to the South Kalimantan city of Banjarmasin, it said.

item.title: Obama appelle à la prudence face à l'IA, exhorte les démocrates à s'attaquer au sujet-presse
item.description: L'ancien président américain Barack Obama a averti que l'intelligence artificielle pourrait s'avérer "dangereuse" si elle n'était pas correctement gérée et a exhorté les démocrates à définir des programmes politiques et de gouvernance pour faire face à ce problème, rapporte dimanche le New York Times.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'ancien président américain Barack Obama a averti que l'intelligence artificielle pourrait s'avérer "dangereuse" si elle n'était pas correctement gérée et a exhorté les démocrates à définir des programmes politiques et de gouvernance pour faire face à ce problème, rapporte dimanche le New York Times. Cette prise de position, formulée lors d'une récente collecte de fonds privée, intervient alors qu'un nombre croissant de législateurs américains réclament un durcissement de la réglementation sur les systèmes d'IA à la suite de mises en garde de deux chercheurs d'Anthropic selon lesquels les progrès rapides du secteur risquent d'entraîner l'extinction de l'humanité. "C'est un domaine qui évolue très rapidement dans le secteur privé, et si nous ne prenons pas les choses en main, je pense que cela peut être dangereux", a déclaré Barack Obama jeudi, selon New York Times. S'appuyant sur une transcription partielle de ses propos fournie par le bureau de Barack Obama, le journal ajoute que celui-ci a encouragé le chef de file de la minorité à la Chambre des représentants, Hakeem Jeffries, à contribuer à l'organisation d'un débat public sur la politique en matière d'IA si les démocrates reprennent la majorité à la Chambre lors des élections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre. "Une fois élu président de la Chambre, je vous encouragerais vivement à ce que les démocrates mettent en place un cadre pour un débat public très visible", a déclaré Barack Obama à Hakeem Jeffries, rapporte le New York Times. L'ancien occupant de la Maison blanche a également appelé les candidats à la présidentielle de 2028 à faire de l'IA l'un de leurs axes prioritaires, avec un plan très clair pour répondre aux préoccupations en matière de sécurité et d'économie qu'elle suscite, précise le journal. Le bureau de Barack Obama n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat répondu à une demande de commentaires de Reuters. Les craintes relatives au secteur ont été alimentées ces dernières semaines par des cas d'agents d'IA devenus incontrôlables et ayant piraté des systèmes externes, ainsi que par le départ de chercheurs spécialisés dans la sécurité de l'IA inquiets des risques liés à cette technologie. Le directeur général d'Anthropic, Dario Amodei, [USN:L6N454074 TEXT:"a appelé samedi"] les entreprises spécialisées dans l'IA à ralentir le rythme auquel elles améliorent les capacités de leurs modèles, avec un cadre en trois étapes visant à modérer leur développement et à gagner du temps pour gérer les risques associés à celui-ci.

item.title: Russian nuclear head says Ukraine attacked fuel trucks, endangered Zaporizhzhia plant
item.description: The head of Russia's state nuclear energy corporation accused Ukraine on Sunday of attacking diesel fuel trucks, killing two Russian servicemen and deliberately jeopardising safety at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The head of Russia's state nuclear energy corporation accused Ukraine on Sunday of attacking diesel fuel trucks, killing two Russian servicemen and deliberately jeopardising safety at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine. Alexei Likhachev said the attack took place on Friday and also resulted in injuries to other Russian soldiers. The Zaporizhzhia plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, was seized by Russian forces in the early weeks of the Ukraine war that broke out in February 2022. Each side has regularly accused the other of actions that endanger safety at the plant and increase the risk of a nuclear accident. Likhachev issued a statement saying Ukrainian forces had launched "a series of combined strikes" on Friday on fuel trucks which deliver diesel to the station. "The strikes hit very close to the perimeter of the station's site," he said. "Two servicemen were killed, and a large number of Russian soldiers were injured, some seriously. They were all involved in supporting this purely civilian mission." Fuel is critically important for the plant as diesel generators provide power to keep nuclear fuel in the reactors cool when the plant's two external power links are down. [USN:L1N44Z0GF TEXT:"Both were down"] for nearly three weeks in August and September. Ukraine has demanded that Russia abandon the station and hand its operation back to Kyiv, a demand rejected by Moscow. The fuel currently generates no electricity. The U.N. nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency, has stationed an observer team permanently at the station, along with Ukraine's three other working plants. The agency has repeatedly acted as an intermediary when disputes arise and last month helped [USN:L1N44X03J TEXT:"arrange a local ceasefire"] in order to carry out repairs and restore external power links.

item.title: Philippine ferry fire victims may take months to identify, authorities say
item.description: Authorities in the Philippines said on Sunday it could take weeks or months to identify the victims of a ferry fire that killed 76 people, as forensic experts begin collecting and comparing DNA samples from charred remains and investigators determine what caused one of the country's deadliest maritime disasters in recent years.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Portugal, Eloisa Lopez
item.content:encoded: Authorities in the Philippines said on Sunday it could take weeks or months to identify the victims of a ferry fire that killed 76 people, as forensic experts begin collecting and comparing DNA samples from charred remains and investigators determine what caused one of the country's deadliest maritime disasters in recent years. Some remains were found clustered together in parts of the vessel, said forensic specialist Richard Allan Mangalip from the Philippine National Police, while others were scattered across different areas of the ship, which was carrying more than 130 people and was nearing its destination when it caught fire. The ferry was heading southwest from Manila to Coron, in Palawan province, a trip that generally takes about 20 hours. "Most of them are already in a charred condition," Mangalip said at a press conference, adding that authorities could not provide a firm timeline for identification because of the volume of specimens that must be examined. "It could be weeks, or it could be much longer." That assessment came a day after rescuers [USN:L6N45403P TEXT:"recovered 41 additional remains"] from the ferry, raising the death toll to 76 and leaving 13 people unaccounted for. Officials said more remains could still be found because investigators have not yet fully searched flooded sections of the vessel. Firefighters entered the ferry for the first time on Friday after extinguishing the blaze more than a day after it broke out. Images released by the Coast Guard showed the scale of the destruction inside the vessel, with rows of steel bed frames twisted by intense heat and covered in ash. Investigators said they had yet to determine where the fire started and were still trying to access key sections of the vessel, including flooded lower decks and the engine room, where evidence may help establish the cause. A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority, citing survivor accounts, said two explosions were heard inside the vessel shortly before the fire broke out. A representative of shipowner Atienza Inter-Island Ferries said at the same press conference the company was cooperating fully with investigators and would continue assisting affected families. The fire is the latest in a string of deadly maritime accidents in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands, where millions rely on ferries and small boats to travel.

item.title: German firms lift China investment as US outlays fall, IW study shows
item.description: German companies increased investment in China by a third in the first half of 2026 while sharply reducing investment in the United States, according to a study by the German Economic Institute (IW) seen by Reuters on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German companies increased investment in China by a third in the first half of 2026 while sharply reducing investment in the United States, according to a study by the German Economic Institute (IW) seen by Reuters on Sunday. German firms invested €5.6 billion ($6.50 billion) more in China than in the same period of the previous year, based on IW's analysis of Bundesbank data. The figure was in line with the average half-year investment level between 2020 and 2025. "German companies have little choice but to continue investing in China," IW's Juergen Matthes said, describing the country as both an important sales market and a "gym" where companies can build up their competitive muscle. Matthes said state subsidies and an undervalued yuan made production in China artificially cheap, encouraging German companies to expand locally to compete with Chinese rivals globally. "For Germany, this means production and jobs are shifting to China," Matthes said. "The EU should put a stop to this unfair game and impose countervailing tariffs on Chinese imports." Investment in the U.S. fell by nearly two-thirds to around €4.3 billion, the study said, amid trade tensions and U.S. tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump. ($1 = 0.8615 euros)

item.title: Campeón Cruz Azul vence al América en clásico del torneo mexicano
item.description: Cruz Azul, vigente campeón del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado por 4-3 al América en uno de los clásicos que enfrentó a dos de los clubes más populares del país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cruz Azul, vigente campeón del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado por 4-3 al América en uno de los clásicos que enfrentó a dos de los clubes más populares del país. La "Máquina Celeste" venció a las "Águilas" con goles de Erik Lira, del argentino José Antonio Paradela, Jesús "Chiquete" Orozco y del uruguayo Gabriel "Toro" Fernández. Para América anotaron el uruguayo Brian Rodríguez, y los colombianos Óscar Perea y Miguel Borja. Cruz Azul tomó el control del partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, y se puso en ventaja a los 19 minutos con un potente y colocado disparo de Lira dentro del área, metiendo el balón por el ángulo derecho tras recibir un pase de Paradela, quien marcó el segundo gol a los 35 con un potente zurdazo en el área tras controlar un pase de Carlos Rodríguez. Tres minutos después, el portero colombiano Kevin Mier evitó el gol del América al desviar un peligroso remate de cabeza de Henry Martín. La situación para América empeoró a los 41 minutos cuando el árbitro Luis Enrique Santander marcó penal a favor de Cruz Azul tras revisar en el VAR una jugada donde el defensor Ramón Juárez derribó dentro del área a Paradela con una falta por atrás. Pero dos minutos después, el portero Rodolfo Cota atajó el tiro penal del argentino Nicolás Ibáñez. A pesar del penal fallado, Cruz Azul siguió buscando el tercer gol que consiguió al minuto 45 cuando Orozco remató en el área chica un tiro de esquina enviado desde el sector derecho. Un minuto después, América estuvo cerca de anotar con un disparo del brasileño Raphael Veiga que pegó en el poste izquierdo. En la segunda parte, América salió a presionar en busca del gol que estuvo cerca de lograr a los 50 minutos con un remate de cabeza de Juárez que pegó en el poste izquierdo. El equipo dirigido por el uruguayo Guillermo Almada consiguió el descuento a los 52 minutos cuando el delantero uruguayo Brian Rodríguez metió el balón por el ángulo derecho al cobrar un tiro de castigo desde fuera del área. Pese a la presión de América, Cruz Azul logró el cuarto gol a los 72 minutos cuando el "Toro" Fernández definió de derecha tras eludir al portero después de recibir un largo pase de Lira. Cerca del final, América marcó el segundo gol con un zurdazo de Perea a los 90 minutos. En la siguiente jugada, Borja metió el tercer gol al definir de derecha después de que Mier rechazó débilmente un potente disparo de Alejandro Zendejas. Con su quinto triunfo, Cruz Azul llegó a 15 puntos para subir del octavo al tercer lugar general, por abajo de Toluca y América, que registran 16 unidades cada uno. En los otros partidos del sábado, Toluca goleó por 5-2 al Atlas con tantos de Alexis Vega, Jesús Angulo, del uruguayo Federico Viñas, del portugués Paulinho y del zaguero Jorge Rodríguez en su propia portería. Para los "Rojinegros" del Atlas anotaron el argentino Florián Monzón y el caboverdiano Luis De Barros "Duk". En tanto, Monterrey y Tigres UANL empataron 0-0. El domingo, Guadalajara enfrentará a Pumas UNAM, mientras que Santos Laguna jugará ante Bravos de Ciudad Juárez. La jornada se completará el lunes cuando León sea local ante el Atlético de San Luis. El viernes, Pachuca goleó como visitante al Atlante por 3-0, Puebla venció por 1-0 como visitante a Necaxa, mientras que Querétaro ganó por 1-0 en su visita a Tijuana.

item.title: Canadiens sign veteran F Chris Kreider to 1-year deal
item.description: Veteran forward Chris Kreider didn't stay a free agent long, signing a one-year contract with the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday, the team announced.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Veteran forward Chris Kreider didn't stay a free agent long, signing a one-year contract with the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday, the team announced. Financial terms were not disclosed, but ESPN reported that Kreider's deal has a $2.15 million average annual value and could be worth as much as $5 million next season if certain conditions are met. The Anaheim Ducks terminated Kreider's contract on Thursday, one day after the 35-year-old went unclaimed on unconditional waivers. Kreider, a Massachusetts native, reportedly was looking to sign with a team in the East. He had one season left -- at a $6.5 million average annual value against the salary cap -- on a seven-year, $45.5 million extension he signed while with the New York Rangers in February 2020. The Ducks said the move gives them more financial flexibility under the salary cap. They are trying to re-sign restricted free agent forward Cutter Gauthier, 22, who led the team with 41 goals and 69 points last season. "I want to thank Chris for his efforts last year and recognize the professionalism he and his representatives demonstrated throughout this process," Anaheim general manager Pat Verbeek said in a statement Thursday. "Our rationale here is straightforward: We needed to create salary-cap flexibility, and this accomplishes that." The Ducks matched a five-year, $90 million offer sheet sent to star center Leo Carlsson by the Philadelphia Flyers in July -- with his $18 million average annual value now the third highest for any NHL player this coming season. The team also signed forward A.J. Greer to a four-year deal and defenseman Pavel Mintyukov to a five-year contract this summer. Kreider recorded 50 points (22 goals, 28 assists) in 75 games during his only season with Anaheim in 2025-26. He added seven points (two goals, five assists) in 12 playoff games. He played his first 13 NHL seasons with the New York Rangers, who drafted him in the first round (19th overall) in 2009. He has 632 points (348 goals, 284 assists), 609 penalty minutes and a plus-117 rating in 958 career games with New York (2012-25) and Anaheim. Kreider led the NHL with 26 power-play goals and 11 game-winning goals during the 2021-22 season, when he scored a career-high 52 goals. The Rangers traded him to the Ducks in June 2025 with a fourth-round draft pick for forward prospect Carey Terrance and a third-round selection that year. Kreider has 83 points (50 goals, 33 assists) in 135 career playoff games. He was a teammate on the Rangers in 2013-15 with Martin St. Louis, now the Canadiens' coach. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sainz to start home Spanish GP 20th after three-place grid penalty
item.description: Carlos Sainz will start the Spanish Grand Prix 20th on the grid on his home turf after receiving a three-place penalty for impeding Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas in Saturday's qualifying session.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Carlos Sainz will start the Spanish Grand Prix 20th on the grid on his home turf after receiving a three-place penalty for impeding Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas in Saturday's [USN:L6N45404Y TEXT:"qualifying"] session. The 32-year-old Williams driver was penalised for impeding Bottas through Turns 6 and 7 during the first phase of qualifying. "The team failed to inform the driver of Car 55 about Car 77 closing in on a flying lap and the driver did not take any action to make way for the incoming car," the FIA said in a statement. "The Stewards determine that Car 55 unnecessarily impeded Car 77." The penalty drops Sainz to 20th on the grid and moves fellow Spaniard Fernando Alonso of Aston Martin, Cadillac's Sergio Perez and Bottas up one place each for Sunday's 57-lap race, the first Formula One grand prix to be held at the Madring. Sainz, a former Ferrari driver and four-time race winner, has endured a frustrating campaign and lies 16th in the drivers' championship with six points. Williams are ninth in the 11-team constructors' standings. Formula One champion Lando Norris secured pole position for McLaren with a superb final lap at the Madring, beating Mercedes championship leader Kimi Antonelli by 0.011 seconds.

item.title: Obama voices caution on AI, urges Democrats to tackle it, NYT says
item.description: Former U.S. President Barack Obama has warned that artificial intelligence could be "dangerous" if not properly managed, and urged Democrats to frame policy and governance agendas to tackle the issue, the New York Times said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former U.S. President Barack Obama has warned that artificial intelligence could be "dangerous" if not properly managed, and urged Democrats to frame policy and governance agendas to tackle the issue, the New York Times said on Sunday. The remarks at a recent private fundraising event come as growing numbers of U.S. lawmakers call for tougher rules on AI systems after dire warnings from two Anthropic researchers that rapid industry progress risks [USN:L6N4520JB TEXT:"extinction of the human race"]. "This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don't get on top of it, I think can be dangerous," the newspaper quoted Obama as saying on Thursday. Citing a partial transcript of remarks from Obama's office, the paper said he encouraged House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries to help shape a public conversation on AI policy if Democrats regained the House in midterm elections on November 3. "Once you are speaker, I would strongly urge that the Democrats put together a framework for a very public conversation," Obama told Jeffries, the paper added. He also called for candidates in the 2028 presidential race to make AI one of their central agendas, with a very clear plan to tackle the surrounding safety and economic concerns, the paper said. Obama's office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The extinction concerns were spurred by cases of AI agents going rogue to hack external systems and AI safety researchers quitting their companies concerned about the technology's risks. On Saturday, Anthropic CEO [USN:L1N45403R TEXT:"Dario Amodei"] urged AI companies to throttle back work on model capabilities amid growing fears of AI misuse, prompting agreement from both OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk, who runs xAI.

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝Ｂジェイズ岡本とＷソックス村上1安打、鈴木は代打で四球
item.description: ［１２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１２日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は１２日、各地で試合を行い、ブルージェイズの岡本和真内野手はオリオールズ戦に「６番・三塁」で出場。２打数１安打、２四球だった。ブルージェイズは７─３で勝利した。

ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手はカージナルス戦に「４番・一塁」で出場。４打数１安打１打点、１得点、１四球、２三振だった。ホワイトソックスは６─５の逆転勝ちを収め、連敗を４で止めた。

カブスの鈴木誠也外野手はパイレーツ戦の八回に代打で出場し、四球で出塁した。カブスは４─３で勝ち、２連勝とした。

item.title: サッカー＝レアルが4得点で快勝、エムバペ2ゴール1シストの活躍
item.description: ［マドリード １２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マドリード　１２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は１２日、各地で試合を行い、レアル・マドリードがキリアン・エムバペの２ゴールなどでラヨ・バリェカノに４─１と快勝した。

レアルは前半１４分にエムバペがＰＫを沈めて先制に成功。その３分後、エムバペのアシストからアルバロ・カレーラスが加点し、同３５分にはジュード・ベリンガムのゴールで突き放した。後半立ち上がりに１点を返されたが、同アディショナルタイムにカウンターからエムバペがこの日自身２得点目をマーク。同選手は今季公式戦６試合で７ゴールとなった。

エスパニョールはロベルト・フェルナンデスの２ゴールでオサスナに２─０と完勝。ラシンはアラベスに２─１で競り勝ち、ビルバオとエルチェは１─１のドローに終わった。

５試合を終えてレアルは勝ち点を１２に伸ばし、翌日に試合を控える首位バルセロナと並んだ。

item.title: ＢＲＩＣＳ首脳、中東に「深い懸念」 共同宣言にイラン・ＵＡＥも署名
item.description:
Sarita Chaganti Singh Shivangi Acharya Saurabh Sharma
[ニューデリー １２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Sarita Chaganti Singh　Shivangi Acharya　Saurabh Sharma

[ニューデリー １２日 ロイター] - 有力新興国で構成する「ＢＲＩＣＳ」は１２日、インドの首都ニューデリーで開幕した首脳会議で中東緊迫について「深い懸念」を表し「最大限の自制」を求める共同宣言を全会一致で採択した。米国と軍事衝突が続くイラン、米国と同盟関係にあるアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）との間で調整が難航すると予想されていたが、初日の採択にこぎ着けたことは両国関係に前向きな兆しと受け止められた。

共同宣言は「対話、協議、外交を通じて」国際紛争を平和的に解決するという加盟国の決意が改めて示された。さらに、米国の対イラン経済制裁やウクライナとの紛争をめぐるロシアへの制裁などに関し、貿易をゆがめる「一方的な関税や非関税措置」の増加についても懸念を表明した。

イランのペゼシュキアン大統領は首脳会議の合間にＵＡＥアブダビ首長国のハリド皇太子と会談。米イランの軍事衝突開始以降では、イラン・ＵＡＥ間で最高レベルでの会談となった。

アブダビの報道担当部門はＸへの投稿で、会談では地域・国際問題や緊張緩和、地域の平和と発展を推進するための取り組みについて協議したと説明した。

イランは軍事衝突開始後、ＵＡＥに繰り返し攻撃を仕掛けており、８月下旬にも米軍部隊やヘリコプターが駐留するアルミンハド空軍基地を標的にした。

在インドのイラン大使館は、ペゼシュキアン大統領とハリド皇太子の会談の写真を掲載。会談内容には触れていない。

中国の習近平国家主席は首脳会議で、中東の和平や安定実現のため「しかるべき役割」を果たす用意があると表明。中国国営中央テレビ（ＣＣＴＶ）によると、「当事者は、政治的解決への取り組みを継続し、恒久的で包括的な停戦の達成に向けて努力しなければならない」と述べた。

item.title: Ticket prices for Shelton-Zverev US Open final down 27%
item.description: The chance to witness tennis history has yet to restoke ticket prices for Sunday's men's final at the U.S. Open in New York.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The chance to witness tennis history has yet to restoke ticket prices for Sunday's men's final at the U.S. Open in New York. Ben Shelton is the first Black American male singles player to reach the championship match since Arthur Ashe in 1972. He will take on No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev at the stadium named after Ashe as Shelton attempts to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick at the U.S. Open 23 years ago. The get-in price for Sunday's final remains steep at $388, according to TicketData.com. However, that does represent a 27% drop over the past three days. The get-in price has remained relatively stable in the 24 hours since Shelton beat fellow American Frances Tiafoe in their primetime semifinal match. The price did drop to $361 on Saturday afternoon before climbing back up to $400 ahead of the latest dip at 11 p.m. ET. The average get-in price through the first 15 days of the tournament has been $246, which is down from $313 at the same point last year, according to TicketData.com. The get-in price for Saturday's women's final between Elena Rybakina and Aryna Sabalenka settled at $314, a 20% drop over the previous three days. Rybakina won her first U.S. Open crown with a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 win over the two-time defending champion. Shelton, 23, is the No. 8 seed and will be playing in his first Grand Slam final. He is 0-5 in his career against Germany's Zverev, 29, who claimed his first Grand Slam title earlier this year at the French Open. All five of their previous meetings came during a 16-month stretch spanning August 2024 to November 2025, and none came in a Grand Slam event. Shelton also is the first Black U.S. man to compete in a Grand Slam final since MaliVai Washington lost in the 1996 Wimbledon final. Discussing his feelings about following Ashe to the U.S. Open championship match, Shelton said, "It's a lot of emotion. My dad, my mom have sacrificed a lot for me to be in this position. ... I'm going to need (the fans) on Sunday to bring the energy. I'm going for it here. I'm gonna leave it all on the court. I hope you guys come and back me. Let's do it for the USA." --Field Level Media

item.title: South Korea wins investment treaty dispute with Chinese investor
item.description: South Korea won a final ruling in a 264-billion-won ($197- million) investor-state dispute after a settlement panel rejected Chinese investor Min Fengzhen's challenge of a 2024 claim dismissal, the justice ministry said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea won a final ruling in a 264-billion-won ($197- million) investor-state dispute after a settlement panel rejected Chinese investor Min Fengzhen's challenge of a 2024 claim dismissal, the justice ministry said on Sunday. The decision represents South Korea's first victory in the full hearing of an international investor claim, the ministry said in a statement. The case centred on Min's claim of violation of protections under an investment treaty between South Korea and China arising from a lender's seizure and sale of pledged shares tied to a failed Beijing property project. The original tribunal dismissed the claim in 2024, saying the investment was illegal and therefore not covered by the treaty. The annulment panel also ordered Min to pay South Korea's legal costs of about 1.5 billion won for the annulment matter, the ministry said. ($1=1,341.4600 won)

JAKARTA, Sept 13 (Reuters) – Indonesian rescuers were searching on Sunday for 140 people from a passenger ship that was earlier reported missing in the Java Sea after 103 others were evacuated, one of whom died, a search and rescue agency official said.

An Indonesian passenger ship carrying 243 people was reported missing after losing contact early on Sunday during bad weather, the search and rescue agency said.

The Virgo Transport 8 ship set sail on Saturday from the East Java city of Surabaya to the South Kalimantan city of Banjarmasin before losing contact, the agency said.

Show Full Article

I Putu Sudayana, the head of the agency’s Banjarmasin office, said in a video statement that 103 people had been evacuated using different ships and some of them would be taken to an East Java port.

Rescuers launched a search, deploying a team, ships and a helicopter toward the passenger vessel’s last known position, he said, without stating what happened to the ship.

Indonesia, an archipelago of 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries as a key mode of transportation, with sea routes more affordable and readily available than air travel.

However, safety standards are not always rigorously enforced, resulting in a relatively high accident rate.

(Reporting by Stanley Widianto; Editing by Jamie Freed)

item.title: Root pleased with England's response to 'unusual summer'
item.description: England have responded excellently to an "unusual summer" marked by a captaincy change, a new coach and off-field incidents, Test captain Joe Root said after his side completed a 3-0 series shutout of Pakistan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England have responded excellently to an "unusual summer" marked by a captaincy change, a new coach and off-field incidents, Test captain Joe Root said after his side completed a 3-0 series [USN:L6N45403K TEXT:"shutout of Pakistan"]. The 35-year-old Root, the second-highest run-scorer in Test cricket history, [USN:L1N43W0FU TEXT:"returned as England Test captain"] after all-rounder Ben [USN:L4N43002A TEXT:"Stokes retired from international cricket"]. Root led England in a record 64 Tests between 2017 and 2022, winning 27 of them. Former New Zealand batter Stephen Fleming was appointed head coach in July following the [USN:L6N43E059 TEXT:"sacking of compatriot Brendon McCullum"] after a four-year stint. The build-up to the second Test against Pakistan was [USN:L1N44K037 TEXT:"overshadowed by controversy"] surrounding fast bowler Brydon Carse, who was [USN:L1N44L0L6 TEXT:"dropped from the England squad"] following an incident outside a nightclub in Derby. Despite the distractions, England completed the sweep on Saturday, sealing an eight-wicket victory in the third and final Test at Edgbaston. "There's been a lot of chaos around this series before a ball was bowled," Root said at a press conference. "At the start of the series, we wanted 3-0 and we've been clinical enough to do that. "It's been a very unusual summer, hasn't it? That's probably a better way of putting it. There's been a lot of different things happen. We had a resignation mid-series, there has been a few off-field incidents and we've got a new coach. "Whether you call it chaos, whether you call it unusual, whether you call it unsettling, all are fair. But ultimately, the thing that I care about, and that's most important, is what happens from that. And I think the way that we've responded to that has been excellent. "And the fact that there's now clarity in what is expected of the group moving forward is quite evident and we build on that now." England next host Sri Lanka in a three-match Twenty20 series beginning in Southampton on Tuesday before facing them in three One-Day Internationals.

item.title: Randal Grichuk's 9th-inning homer lifts White Sox past Cardinals
item.description: Randal Grichuk hit a go-ahead two-run home run with two outs in the top of the ninth inning Saturday night for the Chicago White Sox, helping them beat the St. Louis Cardinals 6-5 and snap a four-game losing streak.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Randal Grichuk hit a go-ahead two-run home run with two outs in the top of the ninth inning Saturday night for the Chicago White Sox, helping them beat the St. Louis Cardinals 6-5 and snap a four-game losing streak. Grichuk went deep with a 1-2 count against closer Riley O'Brien, taking a sinker just over the fence to the opposite field in right, with outfielder Victor Scott II also losing his glove over the fence. Grichuk's 13th home run, against the team that brought him to the majors, trumped a tie-breaking solo shot by Cardinals rookie Leo Bernal against Grant Taylor in the bottom of the eighth. The White Sox (76-72) increased their lead in the AL Central over Cleveland to 1 1/2 games after the Guardians fell 4-3 at Minnesota. The White Sox, trying to make the playoffs after losing at least 100 games in three straight seasons, had led the division by 5 1/2 games before dropping nine of 12. Another former Cardinals player, right-hander Jordan Hicks (3-2), walked a batter but also got one out for the victory. Bryan Hudson got three outs for his eighth save, including a strikeout of pinch-hitter Jordan Walker. Kyle Teel worked a leadoff walk in the ninth against O'Brien, with Brenton Doyle pinch-running for Teel and stealing second base on a pitchout after one out. Doyle initially was called out at second but shortstop Masyn Winn dropped Bernal's throw on the tag at the bag. One out later, Grichuk came to the rescue. O'Brien (3-8) blew his eighth save in 44 chances for the Cardinals (73-76), who have lost six of nine to fall 7 1/2 back of the last National League wild-card spot. The White Sox went 3-for-11 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine, squandering seven walks and three hit batters by Cardinals pitchers. Chicago went 0-for-8 with 12 left on base in the series opener. The White Sox overcame another poor outing from right-hander Luis Castillo, who allowed three runs, four hits and three walks in 2 2/3 innings of relief. Winn had two hits and drove in a pair of runs for the Cardinals, who also got three hits from Nathan Church. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ｆ１＝スペインＧＰ予選で角田15番手、ノリスがＰＰ獲得
item.description: ［マドリード １２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［マドリード　１２日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１のスペイン・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は１２日、マドリードの新設半市街地コース「マドリング」で予選を行い、レーシングブルズの角田裕毅は１５番手だった。

昨季の総合王者ランド・ノリス（英国、マクラーレン）が今季３回目、通算１９回目のポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）が０．０１１秒差の２番手となり、マックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ、レッドブル）が３番手に入った。

ルイス・ハミルトン（英国）が４番手、シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）が５番手とフェラーリ勢が続き、総合２位のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）は６番手、オスカー・ピアストリ（オーストラリア、マクラーレン）は７番手。

レーシングブルズのもう１台、アービッド・リンドブラッド（英国）は１０番手だった。

item.title: サッカー＝鈴木フル出場のアストンビラ、今季初得点も勝利ならず
item.description: ［ロンドン １２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ロンドン　１２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは１２日、各地で試合を行い、ＧＫ鈴木彩艶がフル出場したアストンビラはノッティンガム・フォレストに１─２で敗れた。

アストンビラは後半１分に先制点を献上。その後、今季リーグ戦初ゴールを奪って同点に追い付いたが、同４３分に決勝ゴールを決められた。アストンビラは開幕４試合で未勝利。守田英正が所属する昇格組のハルはチェルシーと２─２で引き分けた。守田はベンチ入りしなかった。

クリスタルパレスはイプスウィッチに２─３で敗れた。クリスタルパレスの鎌田大地は先発し、２アシストをマーク。後半３９分までプレーした。同僚の冨安健洋は前半３７分から出場。イプスウィッチの前田大然は後半１８分からピッチに入った。

遠藤航が所属するリバプールはフラムとスコアレスドロー。遠藤はベンチ入りしたが、出番はなかった。昨季王者アーセナルはサンダーランドを２─０で下し、開幕４連勝。後半１３分に新戦力ブルーノ・ギマランイスの初ゴールで先制し、アディショナルタイムにブカヨ・サカがＰＫで追加点を挙げた。

トットナムはエバートンと０─０の引き分けに終わった。トットナムがリーグ戦開幕４試合を全て無得点で終えたのは球団史上初めて。

item.title: Myanmar government revokes status and seeks action against UN envoy Kyaw Moe Tun
item.description: Myanmar's military-backed government said on Sunday its permanent representative to the United Nations was undertaking "illegal activities" and that his status had been revoked and withdrawn.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Myanmar's military-backed government said on Sunday its permanent representative to the United Nations was undertaking "illegal activities" and that his status had been revoked and withdrawn. Here are some other details of the situation surrounding UN permanent representative Kyaw Moe Tun: The government said, according to a statement issued by state media, Kyaw Moe Tun was dismissed from the civil service on February 27, 2021, for failing to follow instructions. On February 26, 2021, Kyaw Moe Tun made [USN:L4N2KW4QT TEXT:"an emotional appeal"] to the UN, urging the international community to not legitimize the military, which seized power in a coup. Kyaw Moe Tun was [USN:W1N2LN02M TEXT:"appointed"] by the previous government, led by Aung San Suu Kyi, which was deposed in the 2021 military coup that triggered civil war across the country. Kyaw Moe Tun's [USN:L8N2UP52G TEXT:"status"] as Myanmar's permanent representative has remained unchanged because the UN Credentials Committee has deferred a decision on Myanmar's representation. The UN Credentials Committee is expected to meet following the UN General Assembly in New York later this month, where it could discuss disputes over representation. Pro-democracy groups and the parallel civilian government, the National Unity Government (NUG), have helped Kyaw Moe Tun retain his position through [USN:L1N2PE0DQ TEXT:"international advocacy"] and lobbying campaigns. Myanmar's military authorities have accused him of unauthorized use of state property and mission funds while working with the NUG. The Myanmar government said it is working through INTERPOL, the United States National Central Bureau, American agencies and diplomatic channels to seek legal action against him.

item.title: Wyatt Langford sparks 6-run fifth as Rangers top D-backs
item.description: Wyatt Langford hit a 435-foot homer to open a six-run fifth inning, Elias Diaz had three hits and an RBI, and the Texas Rangers beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 6-2 on Saturday in Phoenix to even a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Wyatt Langford hit a 435-foot homer to open a six-run fifth inning, Elias Diaz had three hits and an RBI, and the Texas Rangers beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 6-2 on Saturday in Phoenix to even a three-game series. Rangers right-hander Nathan Eovaldi, activated from the injured list Saturday, gave up one run over 2 2-3 innings of relief in his first appearance since Aug. 7, though he did not factor in the decision. Eovaldi entered in the sixth with a 6-1 lead and made his first regular-season relief appearance since Aug. 14, 2019, while with Boston. Jacob Latz got the last four outs. Brandon Nimmo had two doubles and an RBI and Josh Jung had two hits and an RBI. Jung was also activated from the injured list Saturday after being out with a left calf strain since July 21. Langford added a double. Tim Tawa tripled and scored, while Pavan Smith and Corbin Carroll had RBIs for the D-backs, who had won five of six. Texas had lost three in a row and five of seven. The Rangers (73-76) gained a game in both the American League West and wild card races. They are two games behind Houston (75-74) in the division and two behind Cleveland for the third AL wild card spot. Texas DH Joc Pederson was struck by a pitch on the right wrist in the fifth and left for a pinch-hitter in the sixth. He missed two months last season with a fractured right hand. D-backs starter Brandon Pfaadt (7-3) gave up six runs and 10 hits in 6 2-3 innings, with seven strikeouts and no walks. The D-backs had won 11 of his last 13 starts. The D-backs (79-70) are 1 1/2 games behind San Diego (80-68) for the third NL wild card spot. The Chicago Cubs (83-66) are one game ahead of Philadelphia (82-67) for the top spot. Texas starter Kumar Rocker gave up one run on two hits in four-plus innings, leaving after walking two to open the fifth with a 6-1 lead. Robert Garcia (1-1) got the next three. Rocker struck out five and walked two. Tawa tripled and scored on Pavin Smith's single for a 1-0 lead in the third. The Rangers had six hits in their six-run fifth. Langford homered before Jake Burger singled, stole second and scored on Diaz's single. After Pederson was hit by a pitch, Corey Seager hit a grounder to first that forced Pederson at second. Pfaadt took a throw at first for a potential inning-ending double play, but after a review, he was deemed to be off the bag. Jung followed with a two-out RBI single, Nimmo added an RBI double and Duran capped the inning with a two-run single. Corbin Carroll's sacrifice fly made it 6-2 in the sixth. --Field Level Media

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urges AI companies to slow model development amid misuse fears

In an essay shared on X, Amodei proposes independent safety evaluators, AI industry coordination as recent misuse and hacking incidents raise concerns over unchecked AI development.

Reuters

13 September, 2026 09:05 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei, addresses the gathering at the AI Impact Summit, in New Delhi, India, February 19, 2026. REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence, outlining a three-step framework intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks.

“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” Amodei wrote in a lengthy essay shared on X on Saturday.

Amodei’s three-step plan calls for embedded independent evaluators with employee-like access to verify safety practices, coordination among frontier AI firms to set safety standards and limit unchecked AI development, and international cooperation to manage AI risks.

Show Full Article

Both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, said in posts on X that they agree with Amodei. “Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same,” Altman said, adding that more information would be shared soon.

Amodei made his essay public after San Francisco-based  Anthropic  released a threat intelligence report on Thursday detailing how several actors had used its Claude AI models for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.

Amodei pointed to AI’s growing ability to improve itself, highlighting long-held concerns about it outpacing human ability to control operation along with the recent incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face as his primary reasons to put the brakes on model advances.

‘KILL US ALL’  Alarm about the potential harm from AI grew this week when  Anthropic  researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the “people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Various OpenAI executives have suggested that leading labs should be willing to coordinate a voluntary slowdown if needed to build confidence in their safety measures.

Anthropic  has positioned itself as the more safety-conscious frontier lab, but is not immune to these concerns. Last week it disclosed another instance of an AI model hacking external systems, after a July incident in which some of its Claude models had hacked into the systems of three companies during cybersecurity tests.

“Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6-12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage,” Amodei wrote.

Amodei said he is not calling for halting model training or technical progress, but ensuring that companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third-party evaluators to confirm these steps.

INITIAL PUBLIC OFFERINGS But there is also an enormous amount of money riding on staying ahead. Both OpenAI and  Anthropic  are preparing for blockbuster initial public offerings. Every new capability can help justify future funding rounds, infrastructure commitments or IPOs.

As part of his proposed framework, Amodei said  Anthropic  would install permanent third-party reviewers inside frontier AI companies, with access to relevant tools and internal risk-assessment processes.

Reuters reported last week that a swarm of rogue OpenAI agents hijacked a German website and transformed it into a bulletin board for other AI agents, with the ChatGPT maker’s officials keeping the incident under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the July breach of the open-source repository Hugging Face.

Many incidents in which AI agents from developers such as OpenAI have hacked or attempted to access external systems have heightened concerns over the increasing capacity of AI models and developers’ ability to contain them.

Amodei said AI companies should voluntarily work together to set standards as growing numbers of U.S. lawmakers are calling for new rules to govern AI systems.

CHINA CONCERNS A coordinated approach, Amodei added, would enable leading U.S. AI companies to carry out necessary safety research and safeguards without putting themselves at a competitive disadvantage. Amodei said that such an approach likely would require targeted antitrust exemptions in the United States to permit collaboration in certain areas.

Amodei said any slowdown by democratically governed countries should be limited to preserving the lead U.S. AI firms hold over China, arguing that a Chinese advantage in AI would pose U.S. national security risks.

“Pacing within democracies will be limited by the lead that U.S. companies have over authoritarian regimes, chiefly the Chinese Communist Party,” Amodei wrote.

Amodei called for tighter controls on advanced AI chips, model distillation and theft of model weights to prevent China from narrowing the gap.

“I believe all frontier labs should partner with government to formalize the idea of permanent embedded evaluators to better prevent and document internal alignment incidents like those that have occurred in the last few months, and to implement regulation focused on keeping capabilities in balance with safety,” Amodei wrote.
